output.brief:
The complaints trace to contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique, the new pads or the hill routes. Northfield Motor Services refilled 13 Eastgate vans from an old bulk drum with a missing cap. Two of those vans were filled from a fresh drum. Two vans we tested after complaints had fluid that boils at about 150°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. All 11 vans with complaints were among the 11 filled from that bulk drum. The same drivers had no complaints in other vans, including on Upper Wend, and every van ran Upper Wend a similar number of days. Northfield recommended rechecking the other vans on 25 Sep, and nobody replied. I'm quite confident (roughly 85–90%).

Next steps: take every Northfield-serviced van off the road now. Test and renew its fluid from sealed stock. Also check any other vans serviced by Calder Road Garage, and check the boiling point of fluid in the Eastgate vans that weren't serviced at Northfield. Do not discipline complainers. That would punish people reporting a real safety fault. Retraining everyone would address the wrong cause. Switching pad supplier is unjustified for now. The extra squeal reports are probably because fresh pads were just fitted, and the evidence doesn't show the pads cause braking faults.
